messages:
jamie.ops: compliance ping  we need a tiny 'how to' for team docs: quick CLI example + minimal wording for EU DSARs on audit exports. can we keep it short and action-oriented?
priya.singh: yep. I can draft a one-paragraph blurb and a short shell + jq example for redaction. where should it live? /docs/security/audit-exports/ or a short faq?
alex.chen: put under audit-exports -> 'DSAR and scoped exports' subsection. keep examples practical: many engs use CLI to generate exports.
morgan: technical note: prefer showing strip-by-field with jq or a --strip-pii flag example so that it's copy-pasteable. avoid long pseudocode.
sara.legal: thanks. legal preference: use term "personal data" (GDPR-friendly) rather than PII, and be explicit about what is removed vs what we can provide (metadata like event_type/time ok). also include a short line about retention of the DSAR record itself.
priya.singh: draft blurb: "For Data Subject Access Requests (EU), Redwood will deliver a scoped export of audit events limited to the requested timeframe and event categories. Personal data fields (for example: email, IP address, device identifiers, session cookies) will be removed or irreversibly masked. The export will be delivered over an encrypted channel and a record of the request and delivery will be retained for compliance purposes." ok?
sara.legal: good. one tweak: change "removed or irreversibly masked" to "removed or irreversibly hashed with KMS-managed salt, when masking is justified for operational analysis", and add retention window for the DSAR delivery record: "retain for 6 years".
alex.chen: updated wording in PR.
priya.singh: example CLI and jq redaction we plan to add:
```
# generate scoped export (example)
redwood audit export \
  --start 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z \
  --end 2025-01-31T23:59:59Z \
  --events login,update_api_key \
  --output audit-january.json

# simple field removal with jq (recommended for DSAR delivery)
jq 'map(del(.email, .ip_address, .session_cookie, .user_agent))' audit-january.json > audit-january-redacted.json
```
priya.singh: adding one-line note about verification: "Confirm redacted file contains no tokens or debug dumps before delivery."
morgan: technical caveat: some logs include serialized headers or base64 blobs; recommend a pre-delivery sanity check command we can suggest: `grep -E "token|authorization|cookie" audit-january-redacted.json || true` to catch obvious artifacts. add as optional troubleshooting tip.
sara.legal: fine but phrase as a "compliance checklist" item. also add the short sentence: "If any hashed values are provided, document the justification and salt custody (KMS) in the DSAR record."
priya.singh: I'll add a tiny checklist block under the subsection:
- scope time range and event types
- confirm personal data fields removed/hashed
- verify no debug/system dumps included
- deliver over encrypted channel and record who delivered
- retain DSAR delivery record for 6 years

jamie.ops: can we include a short note for customers: "If you request raw exports for legal purposes, our team will coordinate to provide a scoped, redacted export and a summary of the redaction applied."
alex.chen: added. also included small FAQ link pointer to SOC2 evidence collection page.
docs-bot: PR opened by priya.singh: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4902  adds DSAR CLI + jq examples, checklist, and legal-approved wording. CI: docs-lint passed.
morgan: quick review done, wording fine. one suggestion: add a short example of irreversible hashing command if we want to show how to hash email with openssl HMAC + salt reference.
sara.legal: not necessary in the public docs; we can keep hashing guidance internal. approve public doc as-is.
docs-bot: PR 4902 approved by sara.legal and morgan, merging in 4m unless objections. :white_check_mark:
priya.singh: thanks everyone  follow-up: I'll open a small internal runbook for the ops team with the hashing examples and KMS notes.
